requirement:
`verify` always captures `Some(criterion.version())`. When `load_evidence` loads
an older answer with no known version, `Fingerprinted::version()` returns `None`.
`Record::version` holds the same optional value. In the serialized `revision`
field, a concrete string represents `Some(version)` and `"*"` represents `None`.
rationale:
The tests cover each clause of `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.recorded_criterion_version`. I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not read the implementation or the test helpers.

- **`verify` always captures `Some(criterion.version())`.** In `contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]`, the value returned by `verify` is checked with `value.version().unwrap().as_str() == "v1"`. After `store_evidence` and `load_evidence`, the test also checks `loaded.version() == value.version()`. So the captured `Some` version survives storage into a `Record` and back.
- **Loading an older answer with no known version gives `None`.** In `contracts.rs#fn[wildcard_revision_does_not_supply_other_criteria_or_nodes]`, a persisted record has its `version` set to `None`. The test then loads it and asserts `loaded.version() == None`. It also asserts that the loaded answer is still usable: the output is returned, `is_compatible_with(loaded.version())` holds, and `check_inputs` passes.
- **`Record::version` holds the same optional value, and the `revision` field encodes it.** `storage.rs#fn[record_preserves_the_stored_version_encoding]` deserializes `{"revision": "review-v1"}` into `Some("review-v1")` and `{"revision": "*"}` into `None`. It then re-serializes each record and checks that it equals the original wire value, so both directions of the encoding are checked. It also asserts that `"*"` is not a valid `CriterionVersion`, which keeps `"*"` reserved for `None`.

I found no obligation that lacks a test and no weak assertion. The test items are marked with `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
